newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks end up, Hongkong Electric shines.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks end up, Hongkong Electric shines.

text.p: A shining performance by Hongkong Electric and fresh evidence of a buoyant property market boosted Hong Kong stocks to a higher close on Thursday.
The Hang Seng index closed 57.32 points higher at 13,491.56. Turnover was HK$7.61 billion compared to HK$8.61 on Wednesday.

"I think Hongkong Electric is sort of leading the market," said Geoff Galbraith, institutional sales trader at Nava SC Securities. "When you are in a bull market, it is a rotational thing and we are getting back to utilities."
Hongkong Electric ended the session up HK$0.45 at HK$27.10 after hitting a high at HK$27.75 during the day.
China Light closed HK$0.20 higher at HK$34.40.

Analysts said investor interest in laggards had helped lift the two utilities this session. "A lot of properties and banks have already had their run and utilities are laggards," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
Interest in laggards also boosted some red chip counters. Shares in CITIC Pacific ended on a gain of HK$0.70 at HK$40.50.
However, the leading property sector continued to benefit from signs of a buoyant property market.

Shares in Sun Hung Kai Properties rose HK$1.25 to HK$98.00 after the company said on Wednesday it would put 75 more units on sale at its luxury King's Park Villa residential development after 189 flats already on offer drew a strong response.
Cheung Kong gained HK$0.50 to HK$69.50 and Amoy Properties rose HK$0.15 to HK$11.10.
However, New World Development fell HK$0.25 to HK$51.00 and Hysan Development slipped HK$0.20 to HK$29.75.

Shares in China Elegance rose HK$0.175 to HK$4.40. The company said it plans to issue 40 million new shares to Mansyong International Development Ltd at HK$3.95 per share, raising net proceeds of about HK$156 million.
Shares in Swire Pacific rose HK$0.75 to HK$74.00 and Hutchison advanced HK$0.75 to HK$60.50.
Cathay Pacific fell HK$0.05 to HK$12.45. The Hong Kong flag carrier said it aimed to raise air ticket prices by three percent in mid-December.
